description: We are university students who have a passion for learning computer skills and game development. What matters to is to learn and have fun along the way.
summary: Our project is a space-themed video game that lets the player travel across the solar system while thinking and reacting quickly to ensure mission success. It reflects some of the problems faced by real space missions.
details:
The player controls a rocket that traverses through space, avoiding asteroids. Right after starting the game, the player has to make an engineering decision in the form of choosing between a fast rocket with fast fuel drain and a slower rocket with less health but more efficient fuel usage. This decision might mean the success or failure of the mission, depending on the player's playstyle.

The game focuses on 3 realistic limitations that are relevant to real space missions: rocket health, oxygen, and fuel supply. Health decreases when the rocket hits an asteroid, fuel decreases rapidly when the rocket boosts, and oxygen depletes throughout. Returning to Earth refills these resources. Moreover, the game uses a coordinate system where Earth is at (0, 0), allowing the player to return to Earth if lost in space. The player has to constantly evaluate wether continuing to explore in a particular route is worth it or is it smarter to return to Earth to recharge, and a misguided decision can mean gameover.

The goal of the game is to gather data from 8 different bodies/planets while managing the limited resources of the mission. Pressing "E" when near a body displays real planetary data provided by Nasa, and at this point that body is "discovered". The creative aspect of this game is juggling between making the game an educational high-stakes decision-based engineering experience and making it an enjoyable video game with tight mechanics that appeals to younger people who might be interested in space and aeronautics.

The game was created in the game engine Godot. The vast majority of the 2d assets were hand drawn with a drawing tablet using the art software Krita.
